question:
DRAG DROP -
An engineer must authenticate OSPF on interfaces of the Cisco Nexus 9000 Series Switch so that: eth1/1 uses clear text password; and eth1/2 uses encrypted md5 password. Drag and drop the commands from the bottom onto the boxes in the code to complete the configuration. Not all commands are used.
template:
SW1(config)# router ospf 1
SW1(config-router)# interface ethernet 1/1
SW1(config-if)# ip router ospf 1 area 0.0.0.0
SW1(config-if)# ip ospf {{1}}
SW1(config-if)# ip ospf {{2}} 0 P@ssW1
SW1(config)# interface ethernet 1/2
SW1(config-if)# ip router ospf 1 area 0.0.0.0
SW1(config-if)# ip ospf authentication {{3}}
SW1(config-if)# ip ospf {{4}} 3 md5 3 2b7cf4643b66b22
theory: NX-OS OSPF supports two authentication modes per interface: simple (clear-text password) authentication, enabled with ip ospf authentication plus a plain-text authentication key, and MD5 message-digest authentication, enabled by setting the interface's authentication mode to message-digest along with a digest key/MD5 hash value. Configuring eth1/1 for the clear-text form and eth1/2 for the message-digest form on the same OSPF process demonstrates that authentication type is set per interface, not per process, mirroring the general simple-vs-MD5 authentication choice available in OSPF. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 18 - Keychain Authentication concept, applied to NX-OS OSPF)
